summary:
Field Shift – Adapting Farms with NASA Data is a project designed to help farmers make better decisions about what crops to grow and how to maintain healthy soil. It uses NASA satellite data along with local soil details, weather conditions and crop information to suggest suitable crop rotation methods.

Our platform uses AI and machine learning to study changes in rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and vegetation health. It also allows farmers to compare their existing crop rotation with alternative options and understand which methods may help save water, improve soil fertility and reduce environmental risks.

We developed this idea to address the challenges farmers face due to changing weather, water shortages and declining soil health. Our main aim is to make NASA data easier to understand and useful in everyday farming decisions, while helping farmers build more sustainable and climate-resilient farms.
details:
Field Shift is a web-based platform designed to help farmers make better decisions about crop rotation and soil management. It combines NASA satellite observations with local soil information, weather conditions, crop details, and farmers' requirements. The platform studies factors such as rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, and vegetation health to help users understand their land conditions.

Farmers can compare their existing crop rotation with at least two alternative strategies. The system uses AI and machine learning to analyse the available information and explain the possible benefits, risks, and limitations of each strategy. This helps farmers make informed decisions rather than depending only on guesswork.

The main benefits are better water management, improved soil health, reduced climate-related risks, and more sustainable farming practices. The intended impact is to make scientific satellite data easier for farmers to understand and use in their daily agricultural decisions, especially in Karnataka.

We developed the project using Google AI Studio, React, TypeScript, Python, and Supabase. We planned to use NASA Earth observation datasets such as SMAP, GPM, MODIS, Landsat, ECOSTRESS, and NASA POWER. We also use tools such as Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for mapping and data visualisation.

The creative aspect of our project is that it connects NASA satellite data with local farming conditions and crop rotation planning in one platform. Instead of simply displaying weather information, it helps farmers compare different crop rotation strategies.

While developing the idea, we considered farmers' needs, local soil conditions, water availability, crop duration, seasonal changes, climate risks, market opportunities, and affordability. We also considered data accuracy and the importance of local agricultural expert validation. Our goal is to support farmers in building healthier soil and more climate-resilient farms.
